The experience

A new kind of dressing room.

i.

Share your portrait.

One full-body image. Used only for this fitting, dissolved within hours. Seen by no one but you.

ii.

Enter your proportions.

Height, bust, waist, hips. Optional, but used to suggest the most flattering size for you.

iii.

Receive your portrait.

A composed image of you in the gown, on the red carpet. Yours to keep, yours to share.

A note on the image

Quietly composed. Briefly kept. Yours alone.

The image you receive is a composition assembled by a model from a single photograph and a garment portrait. It is an approximation of how the piece would meet your body — not a guarantee of fit.

Your photograph is processed for this fitting only, then dissolved from our system within twenty-four hours. It is never used to train a model, never shared, and never seen by a human — except, briefly, by you.
